findings.summary: Salary calculation imports an unnamed subset of the interactive salary-research prompt instead of a bounded reusable benchmark contract.

assessment.reason: The current read-only warning already prevents intentionally restarting research, and no incorrect result was established. A named reusable boundary would modestly reduce the burden of locating scattered requirements and maintaining their Step 4 restatement; the extra resource/read edge must justify its cost.
evidence: Project guidance in AGENTS.md keeps orchestration in workflows, step behavior in prompts and reusable rules in explicitly loaded flat skills references; this is a project convention, not a framework requirement.

prompts/salary-calculator/step1-research-prompt-generator.md:18 mixes local-employee benchmark scope with employment-path questions; lines 36–49 and 71–90 spread tier, pay-basis, geography/hours and source/method requirements through research instructions and the answer format.

prompts/salary-calculator/step4-table-calculation.md:26 selectively imports only benchmark-scope and benchmark-metadata requirements from Step 1 without named section boundaries, then repeats its comparability checklist. Maintainers must preserve that selective edge whenever these shared requirements change.

prompts/salary-calculator/step5b-final-verification.md:5–9 consumes saved benchmark context and loads Step 4 as the canonical calculation procedure. Existing arithmetic, field formats, question ownership and validation contracts remain intentional.
assessment.invariant: Preserve both independently researched local-employee employer tiers, original research field names and answer format, literal self-contained researcher briefs, role/level/geography/hours/pay/source-method comparability, recoverable legacy metadata without invention or stricter ingestion, qualification and skip rules, question order and choices, checkpoints, profile/state schemas and generated outputs. Keep country selection/research orchestration in Step 1 and calculation eligibility in Step 4.

evidence: Revalidated at a47bda6: the original Step 1 employment-path mixing had already been removed by the fixed benchmark-scope paragraph, so the remaining issue was Step 4's unnamed import.

Step 1 now labels the scope paragraphs 'Benchmark scope:' and Step 4 line 26 enumerates the imported metadata requirements. A static check confirmed each named item exists in Step 1: the single Low/Realistic/Strong amounts bullet, the pay-basis/hours/geography bullet, settled role/level, the source-and-method bullet and the Benchmark basis and Estimate method fields.

This is a prompt-wording change with no model run. Researcher briefs, answer format, question order, calculation rules and Step 5b were not touched, but model behavior was not verified; the optional replay script was not run.

findings.summary: Run workspace workflow validation hides inside a predicate named checkpointed, so four call sites rely on its side effect and every call reparses the registry.

assessment.reason: A reader must know that checkpointed() raises for unknown workflows to understand why start(), list_runs() and catalog() call it and discard the result; separating validation from the checkpoint predicate and loading the registry once per call path would make those call sites self-explanatory and cut the repeated registry reads.
evidence: helpers/compass_lib/runs.py:18-24 defines checkpointed(), which loads and parses data/workspace-files.json, rejects non-string input, returns False for registry profile_workflows and otherwise calls definition() to raise for unknown workflows.

helpers/compass_lib/runs.py:82, 129 and 155 call checkpointed() only to validate the workflow and discard the boolean; only line 138 uses the result. Line 56 in location() parses the same registry file separately, and the catalog call at line 82 reparses it for every saved run.
No other module imports checkpointed(); scripts/test_compass.py already rejects an unknown workflow (portal-finder) at run-start, giving a regression check for the rejection path.
This is a project convention and readability judgment, not a framework requirement or measured performance problem.
assessment.invariant: Preserve run-list, run-start and workspace-base request and response shapes, the exact ValueError messages for unknown, non-string and uncheckpointed workflows, Job Screener as the only profile-only workflow, immutable run metadata validation, and the absence of any new files or dependencies.

evidence: helpers/compass_lib/runs.py now has registry(), require_workflow() and a pure checkpointed() predicate; the three validate-and-discard call sites and the catalog loop call require_workflow(), and location() shares registry(). The duplicated registry path expression is gone.
Registry parsing per call was left unchanged and was not measured; the improvement is naming and removing the hidden side effect, not fewer reads.
In a throwaway copy, making require_workflow() a no-op made test_job_screener_same_person_profile_transfer_keeps_command_baselines_separate fail, so the unknown-workflow rejection is protected.

findings.summary: scripts/test_plugin.rb repeats the same seven-line begin/rescue/ensure rejection check twelve times with hand-varied message matching.

assessment.reason: Each new validator guard has been added by copying the block and editing its matcher and restore step (five of the twelve copies arrived since the last assessment), so the matching rules drift between exact message, prefix and any-error checks and each addition costs more review than the assertion warrants.
evidence: scripts/test_plugin.rb:68, 85, 123, 140, 156, 167, 181, 195, 209, 223, 233 and 263 each assign `rejected = begin; CompassValidation.validate(installation); false; rescue RuntimeError => error; <matcher>; ensure <restore>; end` followed by an assertion.

Matchers differ deliberately: start_with and end_with for missing resources, exact messages for policy checks, and a bare `true` for the icon table at line 263, so a helper must accept the matcher and the restore step rather than hard-code either.
The validate_plugin.rb guards these blocks protect (client manifest parity, commands omission, Desktop-incompatible fields, icon rules) are separately selectable and would stay unchanged.
assessment.invariant: Preserve every existing rejection scenario, its exact expected message or matcher, the restore step that returns the installation to a valid state, the following 'must validate' assertions and the order of mutations; a mutation of each guarded validator check must still fail the corresponding assertion.

evidence: scripts/test_plugin.rb defines one rejected_with helper (exact-message String, lambda or no matcher, plus a restore block that runs even if validation passes) and all twelve rejection checks use it; the file shrank by 68 lines with the same 447 checks.

Every scenario, matcher and restore step was kept. In throwaway fixture repositories, disabling each of the seven exact-message validator guards, and the lazy-QM guard, made the old and refactored tests fail identically; the prefix-matched QM guard ran identically in both.

findings.summary: CompassValidation.validate packs about eight unrelated package checks into one 148-line method, so adding or locating a rule means editing a monolith whose check order and messages 13 mutation tests depend on.

assessment.reason: Manifest parity, icon SVG safety, registry and contract shape, skill and agent frontmatter, link resolution and duplicate-template checks share one scope and one local variable set. A maintainer changing one concern must read the whole method, and the first-failing-check order is an implicit contract; named steps called in the same order would make each concern findable without changing which message a given defect produces.
evidence: scripts/validate_plugin.rb:33-180 defines validate(root) as a single method covering client manifests and marketplace, the icon SVG, helper and registry resources, the output contract, skills, agents, runtime references and docs frontmatter.

scripts/test_plugin.rb uses rejected_with 13 times and several String matchers that compare exact validator messages, so reordering or rewording a check changes which fixture is rejected and with what text.
scripts/validate_plugin.rb run(root) calls validate twice, once on the repository and once on a relocated copy, so any split must keep the same inputs and return value.
scripts/test_plugin.rb currently runs 462 checks including the validator mutations, giving strong regression coverage for a behavior-preserving split.
This is a local readability and change-cost judgment, not a framework requirement.
assessment.invariant: validate(root) keeps its signature and true return value, runs the same checks in the same order, raises the same messages for the same defects, and still validates a relocated package without writing to the consumer workspace.

evidence: scripts/validate_plugin.rb: validate(root) is now a 16-line sequence of named steps (validate_manifests, validate_icon, validate_helper_resources, validate_registry, validate_output_contract, validate_entry_points, validate_question_mechanism, validate_skills, validate_agents, validate_references, validate_docs_frontmatter); the largest step is 28 lines.

The change only moves existing lines under new method names: every check, message and its order is unchanged, and validate still returns true. A line-sequence comparison of the original body against the concatenated steps matched exactly before the commit.
The 13 rejected_with mutation fixtures in scripts/test_plugin.rb still reject with the same exact messages.

findings.summary: scripts/test_compass.py repeats the same non-recursive directory snapshot comprehension 20 times in CompassCLI while only RunWorkspaces has a named snapshot helper.

assessment.reason: Each read-only guarantee test builds its before and after state with an identical inline comprehension; a small named helper would make the intent (nothing in this directory changed) readable at each call site and give one place to adjust the comparison.
evidence: scripts/test_compass.py contains 20 occurrences of {p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in <root>.iterdir()} within CompassCLI tests such as the research-scope, filename-resolution and ingestion cases.
RunWorkspaces already defines snapshot(self, root) at line 1038, but it is recursive and keyed by relative path, so it is not interchangeable and a distinct helper is needed.
The helper suite (105 tests) exercises every occurrence and passes at this snapshot, so the replacement is covered by the same assertions.
Test-quality finding only: it preserves what each test proves and adds no coverage.
assessment.invariant: Each affected test keeps its inputs, assertion operands, ordering and subTest structure; the helper returns the same dict of file names to bytes for the same directory.

evidence: scripts/test_compass.py: the 20 inline directory-snapshot comprehensions in CompassCLI are replaced by one static snapshot(root) helper returning the same non-recursive dict of file names to bytes; no assertion, input or subTest structure changed.
RunWorkspaces keeps its own recursive snapshot helper, which was not interchangeable and was left alone.

findings.summary: scripts/test_plugin.rb opens repository files 25 times with inline read(encoding: ...) in two spellings even though it already loads CompassValidation.read, which does the same with a single encoding.

assessment.reason: Twelve calls use encoding "UTF-8:UTF-8" and thirteen use "UTF-8"; the script already requires validate_plugin and its CompassValidation.read(path) wraps Pathname#read with the explicit UTF-8 pair that the US-ASCII default test relies on. One call form removes the inconsistency and the repeated encoding argument.
evidence: scripts/test_plugin.rb has 25 occurrences of read(encoding: "UTF-8..."): 12 with "UTF-8:UTF-8" and 13 with "UTF-8".
scripts/validate_plugin.rb:21 defines CompassValidation.read(path) as Pathname(path).read(encoding: "UTF-8:UTF-8"), and test_plugin.rb already uses CompassValidation.check and .validate.
scripts/test_plugin.rb lines 33-37 run the validator under US-ASCII defaults, so explicit decoding must remain.
ruby scripts/test_plugin.rb (462 checks) reads every one of these files, so any encoding difference would fail it.
assessment.invariant: Every file is still decoded as UTF-8 regardless of the process default encoding, with identical text for the same inputs and the same assertions.

decision.reason: Developer asked for a recommendation and accepted it: not worth the churn.

evidence: CompassValidation.read(root.join(x)) is no shorter than root.join(x).read(encoding: "UTF-8"), so the only gain is unifying the encoding spelling across 25 call sites.
Some call sites are block calls on a file variable, so a mechanical replacement does not fit all of them.

findings.summary: scripts/test_workflow_replay.py check() is a 102-line function that branches on case["group"] strings, so each replay scenario's assertions are interleaved with the others and cannot be read or extended independently.

assessment.reason: Replay, JD, portal, visa and no-adjustment scenarios share one scope of derived lists (messages, writes, operations, handoffs, questions) and one nested if chain; per-group functions behind a small dispatch would let a new scenario add its own assertions without reading the others.
evidence: scripts/test_workflow_replay.py:242-343 defines check(case, initial, final, trace) with branches for replay, jd and jd-next, portal and portal-supplied, visa-annual, visa-incomparable, visa-pending and a final else for no-adjustment.
main() also calls check() on saved prior evidence for the successive-JD case, so its signature is used in two places.

The script is optional acceptance tooling that calls Claude or Codex models, is not part of rake test and has no offline test, so equivalence can only be shown by the same replays or by a separately scoped offline test.
assessment.invariant: check() keeps its signature, evaluates the same assertions with the same messages for each group, and the unexpected-fixture-change guard still runs for every case.

blocker.reason: The replay script needs the Claude or Codex CLI, calls a paid model and is outside rake test, so an offline equivalence check does not exist; a behavior-preserving split cannot be verified without those replays or a separately scoped offline test.
